title: Portrait and Ledger
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Vasse is exhumed for a centennial reinterment and found empty, concierge Rafael Pemberton is drawn in because the only witness to the original 1924 burial was a hotel bellhop — Rafael's own grandfather, whose diary Rafael has quietly kept for years. As Rafael investigates, they discover the founder faked his death to flee with embezzled town funds, and that someone alive today has been killing to keep that secret buried. The killer turns out to be the town archivist, Marisol Quist, who learned the truth through the very ledgers she curates and has eliminated three people who touched the file. At the anniversary dinner, Rafael traps her by publicly reading the grandfather's diary aloud, forcing her confession before the toast is raised.
about_author: O. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk at a grand seaside hotel who spent a decade listening to guests lie beautifully. They now write mysteries from a small apartment overlooking a harbor they no longer trust.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Brass
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Rafael Pemberton, who watches from the hotel lobby as the centennial exhumation draws a crowd — and hears the gasp when the coffin lid opens on nothing. Rafael's pride in noticing everything collides with dread: their grandfather's name appears in the burial record. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: A Concierge Keeps No Files
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Police detective Ilsa Brandt interviews staff; Rafael deflects, but privately retrieves their grandfather Tomas's leather diary from a locked drawer. The 1924 entry describes carrying 'a heavy guest' to the grave at midnight. Beat: loyalty to a dead man versus curiosity he can't suppress.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Marisol Quist, town archivist, graciously helps Rafael access centennial records while steering him away from the financial ledgers. Rafael notices her gloves, her rehearsed warmth, and one ledger page trimmed too neatly. Beat: first flicker of suspicion wrapped in charm.

chapters.title: What the Bellhop Carried
chapters.summary: Tomas's diary, intercut with his 1924 voice via entries. He describes burying sandbags weighted with founder's medals while Vasse himself watched from a waiting car. Rafael realizes the town's founding myth is a fraud. Beat: vertigo as heritage crumbles.

chapters.title: The First to Touch It
chapters.summary: Detective Brandt's POV. A retired gravedigger who handled the exhumation permit is found drowned in shallow water, ruled accidental. Brandt isn't convinced; neither is Rafael, who recalls the man asking odd questions at the desk. Beat: the case turns lethal.

chapters.title: Anniversary Countdown
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Town preparations for the Founder's Anniversary Dinner accelerate; the mayor pressures everyone toward a tidy narrative. Rafael begins mapping who had access to the burial file across a century. Beat: claustrophobia of a small town closing ranks.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. She pulls Vasse's bank records and finds systematic embezzlement hidden as land purchases — and discovers someone requested the same records two months ago under a forged letterhead. Beat: the killer is working the paper trail ahead of them.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Hotel archives reveal Vasse stayed under an alias the week after his 'death,' then vanished. A second diary insert shows Tomas was paid off — and threatened. Beat: grief that his grandfather was complicit, then brave.

chapters.title: Second Grave, Same Silence
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The town historian who authenticated the exhumation request survives a staged fall down archive stairs, hospitalized and mute with fear. She whispers one word to Brandt: 'ledger.' Beat: rising dread, evidence of method.

chapters.title: Quid Pro Quo
chapters.summary: Rafael and Brandt form an uneasy alliance over bad coffee; each holds half a picture. Rafael conceals the diary still, testing whether the detective can be trusted. Beat: wary partnership, guilt sharpening.

chapters.title: The Trimmed Page
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Forensic comparison confirms the archived ledger page was cut with a conservator's blade — a tool only the archivist's office owns. But Rafael also finds Tomas's signature on a hush-payment receipt. Beat: suspicion hardens into certainty, poisoned by shame.

chapters.title: Someone Reads Over Your Shoulder
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Her office is searched overnight; nothing taken, everything photographed. A note left behind quotes her own case notes verbatim. Beat: the hunter realizing she is hunted by someone inside the file itself.

chapters.title: Midnight Reburial
chapters.summary: Rafael stakes out the Vasse mausoleum and catches a figure replacing something in the empty coffin — sandbags, fresh ones. The figure escapes; Rafael recognizes the gait and the glove. Beat: heart-pounding confirmation, but not proof.

chapters.title: The Descendant's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vasse's great-grandson, Aldous, offers Rafael money to stop digging before the dinner — the family fortune depends on the founder's sainthood. Rafael refuses, but realizes Aldous is being manipulated too. Beat: temptation declined, pity kindled.

chapters.title: What Marisol Curates
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Digging into Marisol's past: she is the granddaughter of the accountant Vasse ruined and framed for the embezzlement. Her life's work was restoring the ledgers — until restoration became revenge. Beat: chilling empathy for the killer.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Cross-referencing deaths: the gravedigger, the historian's attack, and a decades-old 'suicide' of a records clerk all connect to ledger access dates. Marisol has been pruning witnesses for thirty years. Beat: horror at the pattern's patience.

chapters.title: Confession in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts Marisol privately in the archive. She admits everything with terrible calm — the town stole her family's name, so she would steal its story back. She knows about the diary and gives Rafael until the dinner toast. Beat: menace wrapped in reasonableness.

chapters.title: Choosing the Trap
chapters.summary: Rafael and Brandt plan: expose Marisol publicly where she cannot silence everyone at once, using the dinner's ritual toast as the trigger. Rafael must finally surrender the diary — and his grandfather's secret — to do it. Beat: sacrifice accepted.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Rafael takes the podium as guest historian, reads Tomas's midnight-burial entry aloud, and reveals the sandbags now sitting in the reopened coffin as physical proof. The room freezes mid-toast. Beat: breathless exposure.

chapters.title: Glass Against Glass
chapters.summary: Climax. Marisol rises, composed, and nearly turns the crowd against Rafael — until Brandt produces the forged letterhead and the conservator's blade. Marisol attempts to leave through the kitchens; Rafael blocks the only exit she didn't memorize. Beat: triumph shadowed by sorrow.

chapters.title: What We Bury, What We Keep
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Aftermath: Marisol confesses fully, insisting the town owed her family a century of interest. The Vasse myth is dismantled; the town grieves its own fiction. Rafael donates the diary to the archive — under new, honest curation. Beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Concierge, Closing Time
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Rafael's POV. Weeks later, a guest asks Rafael if the hotel ever forgets anything. Rafael answers that it remembers everything — the job is deciding what to hand back. The last diary page gets a final entry in Rafael's hand. Beat: quiet restoration of self.
